subject: MAP draft + technical evaluation checklist (post-call)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Eva Morales <eva@healthgrid.com>, Samir Patel <samir@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: MAP draft + technical evaluation checklist (post-call)

Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation with the HealthGrid team. Per our call, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan focused on the technical evaluation milestone so we can keep momentum toward a December close. Key items summarized below.

Summary (high-level)
- Goal: confirm Redwood can meet HealthGrid latency, cost, and quality targets for the clinical documentation pipeline.
- Target close date: 2026-12-20 (proposed in MAP).
- Next milestone: Technical evaluation kickoff (benchmarks + test harness) week of 12/6.

Technical evaluation checklist (draft milestones)
1) Kickoff & test access (owner: HealthGrid - Samir) — 12/06: provide sample dataset, access patterns, and primary evaluation prompts.
2) Benchmark run (owner: Redwood - Priya) — 12/07–12/10: run model shortlist across 512/1k token tails, capture throughput and 95th pctl latency.
3) Quality sweep (owner: HealthGrid / shared) — 12/11–12/13: human pass/fail on clinical hallucination cases & instruction-following.
4) Cost projection & optimization recommendations (owner: Redwood - Marcus) — 12/14: batching/quantization suggestions and estimated $/1k-token.
5) Readout & go/no-go (owners: joint) — 12/16: review results, confirm next-stage plan.

Benchmarks we propose to collect
- 95th percentile generation latency at sequence lengths 256, 512, and 1024 (ms).
- Tokens-per-second / throughput under 2, 4, and 8 concurrent sessions.
- Per-1k-token cost estimate (hosted and dedicated profiles), including quantized variants.
- End-to-end response accuracy on curated clinical prompts (pass/fail + examples).

Initial target thresholds (draft)
- Latency: 95th pctl <= 250 ms for 512-token window (on dedicated GPU profile).
- Throughput: >= 12 tok/s (sustained) for the 512 token benchmark under 4 concurrent sessions.
- Cost: projected <= $0.50 per 1k generated tokens in optimized config (batching + int8).
- Quality: <= 2% critical hallucination rate on the supplied test set.

Model shortlist (first pass)
- owl-v2-13b (quantized 8-bit) — strong instruction following, lower cost.
- openllama-70b-qa (fp16) — baseline quality, higher cost but strong on clinical phrasing.
- redwood-compat-34b (int8) — balanced latency/quality for on-prem.

Dependencies / risks
- HealthGrid to provide representative prompt set + 3k tokens of anonymized examples by 12/03.
- Access to test environment (VPC peering or secure ingestion pipeline) for accurate E2E measurements.
- Any data residency constraints that would force private deployment will change timelines.

Immediate asks (action items)
- Samir: confirm dataset delivery timeline and preferred access method (S3 link or SFTP) by EOD Monday 11/29.
- Eva: approve target close date or propose alternative by 11/30.
- Priya/Rishi: prepare benchmark harness and confirm infra needs by 12/01.

Attachments: HealthGrid_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP draft), hg-technical-benchmarks.xlsx (benchmark matrix), recording-20261128.mp4 (call recording).

Happy to adjust thresholds — this is intentionally conservative to give margin. If it helps, I can map each benchmark to a specific Redwood API/instance type.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Eva Morales <eva@healthgrid.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@healthgrid.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MAP draft + technical evaluation checklist (post-call)

Thanks Marcus — useful summary and appreciated the clear milestones. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Dataset delivery: we can provide a de-identified sample (approx 2k turns, ~1.2M chars) via an S3 presigned link by 12/02. Samir is coordinating.
2) Latency expectations: our clinical workflows are latency-sensitive for live scribing; 250 ms 95th pctl is reasonable but we need a readout at 95th pctl <= 200 ms if we want to avoid UI adjustments. Can Redwood indicate which model/instance pairing you expect will hit 200 ms so we can prioritize?
3) Security: we'll need a SOC2 evidence checklist and confirmation that logs can be retained for 90 days.

We'll plan the technical deep-dive for the week of 12/6. Samir — can you confirm S3 timeline?

—Eva
Eva Morales
Director of Product, HealthGrid
eva@healthgrid.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Eva Morales <eva@healthgrid.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP draft + technical evaluation checklist (post-call)

Thanks Eva — good notes. A few technical commitments up front so expectations are aligned: 

- For a 95th pctl <= 200 ms target on 512 tokens, our likely candidate is redwood-compat-34b running on a dedicated A100-like profile with continuous batching and KV cache enabled. We will validate in the first benchmark run; if E2E network topology increases latency we will propose a dedicated private node during the pilot.
- If HealthGrid is open to INT8 quantized variants, owl-v2-13b (quantized) can often hit sub-200ms for shorter sequences and is significantly cheaper — we will include that in the parallel runs.
- Security: Priya will attach the SOC2 matrix and outline the log retention config (90 days acceptable).

Benchmark specifics we'll deliver in the harness
- Synthetic load generator for 2, 4, 8 concurrent clients (scripts provided).
- 95th pctl measurement computed with warm-up (10k tokens) + steady window (50k tokens).
- Cost model: tooling will output projected $/1k tokens for hosted vs dedicated + sensitivity to batching size.

I will own the technical readout and provide recommended fallbacks if we miss the 200 ms threshold (e.g., alternative model, dedicated node, or partial on-device caching).

Proposed immediate deliverable: Priya and I will share a runnable harness and short README by 12/01. Samir/Eva — if you can confirm S3 access by 12/02 we’ll queue the runs on 12/07.

Onward — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Applied ML | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attached: SOC2_matrix_stub.pdf (sent separately to Eva), benchmark-harness-readme.md (to follow)
